papers.title: scYeast: a biological-knowledge-guided foundation model on yeast single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Though large-scale pre-trained models are vital for foundational cell modeling, most of them focus on human or mouse systems, with less emphasis on model organisms like yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), and fail to use existing biological prior knowledge effectively. Here, we present scYeast, the first foundational cell model for yeast single-cell transcriptomics that effectively embeds biological priors. scYeast employs a novel asymmetric parallel architecture to infuse transcriptional regulatory information into the Transformer's attention mechanism, leveraging biological knowledge during tr
papers.summary: scYeast is the first foundation model for yeast single-cell transcriptomics, incorporating biological prior knowledge through a novel asymmetric parallel architecture that integrates transcriptional regulatory information into the Transformer's attention mechanism. This approach improves cell representation and downstream analysis by leveraging existing biological knowledge, addressing a gap in models focused on non-human organisms.

papers.title: Whole genome sequencing in cerebral palsy: a UK paediatric pilot study.
papers.abstract: Prior international studies indicate that 9-36% of people with cerebral palsy (CP) have a monogenic condition. However, the utility of whole genome sequencing (WGS) as a diagnostic tool for United Kingdom (UK) National Health Service (NHS) patients has not been evaluated.
papers.summary: This pilot study evaluates the diagnostic utility of whole genome sequencing (WGS) in a UK pediatric cohort with cerebral palsy (CP), finding that a significant proportion of cases have an underlying monogenic cause. The results support the integration of WGS into NHS diagnostic pathways for CP.

papers.title: Characterizing highly conserved fragments in 3'UTRs via statistical and transfer learning approaches.
papers.abstract: 3' Untranslated regions (3'UTRs) serve as regulatory platforms that modulate steps in the central dogma through the binding of RNA-binding proteins and miRNAs. Their binding sites are often identified through orthologous regions among species. A separate but related discovery was the ultraconserved elements (UCEs) detected in human, rat, and mouse genomes two decades ago. However, knowledge about their functions is limited. Perplexingly, mutagenesis of UCEs produced no observable phenotypic differences. The majority of UCEs are non-coding, though ∼8% are located in the 3'UTRs. Given the import
papers.summary: This study characterizes highly conserved fragments within 3'UTRs using statistical and transfer learning approaches, building on the concept of ultraconserved elements (UCEs). The authors aim to shed light on the potential regulatory functions of these conserved 3'UTR regions, which have remained poorly understood despite their evolutionary significance.

papers.title: Accelerating inference in genomic and proteomic foundation models via speculative decoding.
papers.abstract: Genomic and protein foundation models (GFMs and PFMs) have demonstrated strong performance in learning the language of DNA and proteins, but their use in large-scale sequence generation is limited by the latency of autoregressive decoding. Because every token triggers a forward pass of a large Transformer, whose inference is relatively slow, long-sequence generation quickly becomes costly.
papers.summary: This paper introduces speculative decoding to accelerate inference in genomic and protein foundation models, reducing the latency of autoregressive sequence generation. By using a smaller draft model to propose tokens and the large model to verify them in parallel, the approach speeds up long-sequence generation without sacrificing accuracy.

papers.title: Transformers for molecular property prediction: domain adaptation efficiently improves performance.
papers.abstract: Over the past six years, molecular transformer models have become a part of the computational toolbox for drug discovery. Most existing models are pre-trained on millions to billions of molecules from large-scale unlabeled datasets such as ZINC or ChEMBL. However, the extent to which such large-scale pre-training improves molecular property prediction remains unclear. This study investigates the potential of transformer models for molecular property prediction while addressing their current limitations. We explore strategies to enhance performance, including the influence of pre-training datas
papers.summary: This study evaluates the effectiveness of transformer models for molecular property prediction and investigates whether large-scale pre-training on datasets like ZINC or ChEMBL improves performance. The authors find that domain adaptation—fine-tuning on task-specific data—efficiently boosts predictive accuracy, addressing limitations of generic pre-training.

papers.title: Histology-derived prediction of a stromal remodeling program in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with transcriptomic and spatial validation.
papers.abstract: To develop and validate a histology-based model for predicting a stromal stiffness-related molecular surrogate in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and to assess its spatial biological plausibility.
papers.summary: This study develops a histology-based model to predict a molecular surrogate for stromal stiffness in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and validates it using transcriptomic and spatial data. The model shows promise as a practical tool for estimating stromal remodeling activity from routine histology slides, potentially aiding in patient stratification.

papers.title: Deep learning-based prediction of drug-target interactions between antiviral drugs and SARS-CoV-2 proteins using an image-based representation approach.
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing offers a time-efficient strategy for identifying therapeutics against emerging pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2. In this study, we apply MPS2IT-DTI (Molecule and Protein Sequence to Image Transformer for Drug-Target Interaction), a deep learning framework that represents molecular (SMILES) and protein (FASTA) sequences as images using k-mer frequency encoding, enabling convolutional neural networks to capture spatial compositional patterns associated with biochemical interactions. A curated dataset (BindingDB-FDA) containing 83,165 binding interactions from 1640 FDA-approved ligan
papers.summary: This study applies a deep learning framework (MPS2IT-DTI) that converts drug and protein sequences into images using k-mer frequency encoding to predict drug-target interactions, specifically for antiviral drugs against SARS-CoV-2 proteins. The approach leverages convolutional neural networks to capture spatial compositional patterns, and the model was trained on a curated dataset of FDA-approved drug interactions, demonstrating potential for drug repurposing.

papers.title: Design of Synthesizable PROTACs through Synthesis Constrained Generative Model and Reinforcement Learning.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis targeting chimeras (PROTACs) have emerged as a promising technology in degrading disease-related proteins for drug design. Recent deep generative models can accelerate PROTAC design, but the generated molecules are often difficult to synthesize. Here, we develop the SynPROTAC model, which integrates chemical reaction path-driven molecule assembly with reinforcement learning for the design of synthesizable PROTACs together with favorable binding properties. Specifically, the synthesis-constrained generative model employs a Graph Transformer-encoded warhead or E3 ligand as input and
papers.summary: The authors developed SynPROTAC, a generative model that combines synthesis-constrained molecule assembly with reinforcement learning to design PROTACs that are both synthesizable and have favorable binding properties. This addresses a key limitation of prior deep generative models that often produce difficult-to-synthesize molecules.

papers.title: SimBinder-IF: Structure-Aware Antibody Affinity Optimization via Efficient Preference Learning.
papers.abstract: Antibody therapeutic efficacy depends on high-affinity target engagement, yet laboratory affinity maturation is slow and costly. Most protein language models (PLMs) lack explicit training for high affinity, and current preference optimization methods introduce computational overhead without clear affinity improvements. Therefore, structure-aware and parameter-efficient approaches for antibody affinity optimization are urgently needed.
papers.summary: This paper introduces SimBinder-IF, a structure-aware method for optimizing antibody affinity using efficient preference learning. It addresses the limitations of existing protein language models and preference optimization methods by incorporating structural information and reducing computational overhead, potentially accelerating the affinity maturation process.

papers.title: EcoXAI: Autonomous Agentic Ecosystem for Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Biomedical Discovery.
papers.abstract: As biomedical datasets and knowledge graphs continue to grow in size, complexity, and heterogeneity, navigating and extracting actionable insights from them presents a major bottleneck for researchers. There is a clear need for autonomous analytical solutions that can utilize recent advancements in agentic AI such as agent harnessing and loop engineering without introducing hallucination or workflow fragmentation. Researchers, regardless of technical expertise, need tools that streamline complex data analysis and deliver meaningful, actionable insights grounded in both data and established bio
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EcoXAI is a new autonomous agentic AI framework designed to make biomedical data analysis more accessible and reliable. It uses multiple AI agents working together to navigate complex datasets and knowledge graphs, aiming to reduce hallucinations and workflow fragmentation while providing explainable insights for biomedical discovery.

papers.title: Omics Data Discovery Agents: Agent-Supported Retrieval, Reanalysis, and Synthesis of Published Omics Data.
papers.abstract: The biomedical literature contains a vast collection of omics studies, yet most published data remain functionally inaccessible for computational reuse. When raw data are deposited in public repositories, essential information for reproducing reported results is dispersed across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and in the rarer cases where intermediate data (e.g. protein abundance files) are shared, their location is irregular. Here we present an agentic framework for the agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data. The system employs larg
papers.summary: This paper introduces an agentic framework designed to improve the retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data, addressing the challenge that most deposited data are not readily reusable due to scattered metadata and irregular file locations. The system uses large language model-based agents to automate the process of finding and integrating data from text, supplements, and repositories, thereby making published omics studies more computationally accessible.

papers.title: Evolutionary, Neural, or LLM-Driven Heuristic Generation? A Unified Ant Colony Optimization Benchmark for Nature-Inspired Routing Heuristics on the TSP and CVRP.
papers.abstract: Biomimetic optimization transfers biological information-processing mechanisms into computational systems. Ant colony optimization (ACO) is a canonical example: artificial ants functionally abstract pheromone-mediated stigmergy, decentralized exploration, trail decay through algorithmic evaporation, and adaptive path reinforcement. Building on this functional biological analogue, we present a controlled cross-paradigm evaluation of routing-heuristic generation. A standardized interface embeds human-designed rules, the genetic programming hyper-heuristic GHPP, a resource-constrained DeepACO-MLP
papers.summary: This paper presents a unified benchmark for comparing different approaches to generating routing heuristics for the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) and Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP), including human-designed rules, genetic programming, and neural/LLM-driven methods. The authors introduce a standardized interface to enable fair cross-paradigm evaluation, providing insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each approach for nature-inspired optimization.

papers.title: AI-Driven Approaches for the Detection, Classification, and Surveillance of Viral Pathogens: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly emerged as a transformative tool in virology, offering new opportunities for the detection, classification, and surveillance of viral pathogens. Recent advances in machine learning, deep neural networks, and multimodal data analysis now enable the identification of viral signatures from genomic sequences, medical images, environmental samples, and social-media-derived epidemiological signals. This review provides a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art AI methodologies applied to viral pathogen research, with a particular focus on image-based diagn
papers.summary: This review comprehensively examines the current state of AI methodologies applied to viral pathogen detection, classification, and surveillance, covering approaches that integrate genomic sequences, medical images, environmental samples, and social-media data. It highlights recent advances in machine learning and deep learning while discussing the challenges and future directions for AI-driven virology, particularly in image-based diagnostics.

papers.title: An Analysis of the Nutritional Value of Diets Generated by Large Language Models Under Average User Conditions-3(LM)Diet Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: AI tools are becoming increasingly common, including in areas related to health and diet. However, there are no studies indicating the nutritional value of diets generated by large language models (LLMs). The aim of this study was to analyse the nutritional value of diets generated by three major language models. Methods: Three LLMs were used in the study: ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot. Using each of these, 35-day meal plans were generated for three energy variants: 2000 kcal, 2500 kcal and 3000 kcal. The meal plans were then analysed using dietary software. Results: All L
papers.summary: This study evaluated the nutritional value of 35-day meal plans generated by three large language models (ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot) across three calorie levels. The findings indicate that LLM-generated diets may not consistently meet nutritional guidelines, highlighting potential limitations in using AI for dietary planning.

papers.title: FoodScribe: an open-source semantic framework for nutrient estimation from free-text dietary records.
papers.abstract: Efficiently summarizing dietary records at scale remains a persistent bottleneck in nutritional epidemiology. We present FoodScribe, which translates free-text meal descriptions into quantitative nutrient profiles by combining ingredient parsing with nutrient retrieval by querying the USDA FoodData Central (FDC) database. Benchmarked using three LLM providers using Nutribench dataset, FoodScribe completed annotation of 3,807 meal descriptions in 2.5 hours, a task otherwise requiring substantial manual effort from trained nutritionists. FoodScribe achieved accuracy across macronutrient estimati
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: FoodScribe is an open-source framework that automatically converts free-text dietary records into quantitative nutrient profiles by parsing ingredients and querying the USDA FoodData Central database. It benchmarked three LLM providers on the Nutribench dataset, completing annotation of 3,807 meal descriptions in 2.5 hours with high accuracy in macronutrient estimation, dramatically reducing manual effort.

papers.title: Computational identification of antigen-specific T cell groups through generative epitope modeling.
papers.abstract: Single-cell T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing enables high-resolution analysis of TCR diversity and clonal expansion. However, inferring antigen specificity for individual TCRs remains challenging and typically requires costly functional assays. We introduce EpitopeGen, a transformer-based model that generates candidate epitope sequences from TCR sequences, enabling population-level identification of T cell groups with shared predicted antigen specificity. EpitopeGen employs a semi-supervised strategy that searches over 70 billion candidate TCR-epitope pairs and incorporates high-confidence bin
papers.summary: EpitopeGen is a transformer-based model that predicts antigen-specific T cell groups by generating candidate epitope sequences from TCR sequences, enabling population-level identification without costly functional assays. It uses a semi-supervised strategy over 70 billion candidate TCR-epitope pairs, offering a computational approach to infer TCR antigen specificity from single-cell sequencing data.

papers.title: Phenotypic Diversity in Multiple Sclerosis Can Be Represented by Four Additive Symptom Modules.
papers.abstract: Background: Multiple sclerosis (MS) lacks a single invariant phenotypic core. Patients accumulate heterogeneous combinations of sensory, motor, cognitive, and autonomic impairments over time, reflecting lesions that are disseminated in time and space. Standard scales such as the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) distribute disability across functional systems, but do not explicitly represent MS phenotype as a mixture of latent symptom modules. Methods: We analyzed 4617 de-identified neurology progress notes from 577 patients with MS at a single academic medical center. A large language m
papers.summary: This study analyzed clinical notes from 577 MS patients using a large language model to identify four additive symptom modules that capture the phenotypic diversity of multiple sclerosis. The findings suggest that MS can be represented as a combination of these latent symptom modules, offering a more nuanced framework than traditional disability scales.

papers.title: A parallel dual-stream state-space module for reliable and efficient biomedical relation extraction.
papers.abstract: Automated drug-drug interaction (DDI) extraction is a cornerstone of global pharmacovigilance, yet its progress is stymied by a fundamental linguistic paradox: relations are signaled by localized morphological cues while being governed by long-range semantic logic. Current monolithic architectures, including Transformer-based models, often face challenges in resolving this feature entanglement, where local clinical descriptors often distort the distal logical chain, leading to noise propagation and reasoning failures. To address this, we present DuSSM, a parallel state-space framework that str
papers.summary: This paper introduces DuSSM, a parallel dual-stream state-space module designed to improve drug-drug interaction extraction by separately handling local morphological cues and long-range semantic dependencies, addressing a key limitation of monolithic Transformer models. The approach demonstrates reliable and efficient performance on biomedical relation extraction tasks.

papers.title: Essentiality-driven prediction of anticancer drug responses in preclinical and clinical contexts.
papers.abstract: Precision oncology relies on tumor molecular profiles to predict drug responses. Instead of using conventional molecular features directly, we construct predictive signatures based on gene essentiality. Here, we present DrGee, an essentiality-centered platform that infers drug sensitivity solely from gene expression profiles. The built-in DeepEEAA model integrates gene expression, gene essentiality, drug-protein affinity, and drug-gene associations to quantitatively predict IC50 values. DeepEEAA achieved competitive predictive performance on independent cell line datasets (R2 = 0.764; MSE = 0.
papers.summary: This paper introduces DrGee, an essentiality-centered platform that predicts anticancer drug responses (IC50 values) from gene expression profiles alone, using a deep learning model (DeepEEAA) that integrates gene essentiality, drug-protein affinity, and drug-gene associations. The model achieves competitive predictive performance on independent cell line datasets (R2 = 0.764), suggesting that gene essentiality can serve as a robust intermediate feature for drug sensitivity prediction in both preclinical and clinical contexts.

papers.title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics for noninvasive risk stratification of pediatric neuroblastoma: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma is the most common extracranial solid tumor in children, with risk stratification guiding therapy and prognosis. Although current risk stratification incorporates imaging-based staging, definitive risk assignment still relies on tissue and molecular characterization, highlighting the need for complementary noninvasive imaging biomarkers. The objectives were to evaluate the classification performance of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics for risk stratification of pediatric neuroblastoma and to determine how MRI sequences, feature-selection methods, and mac
papers.summary: This pilot study evaluates whether radiomics features extracted from multiparametric MRI can noninvasively classify risk groups in pediatric neuroblastoma, potentially reducing reliance on invasive tissue sampling. The authors assess the impact of different MRI sequences and feature-selection methods on classification performance, suggesting that imaging-based biomarkers could complement current risk stratification.

papers.title: EvoSNR-Prom: Predicting promoters at single-nucleotide resolution with label-aware transfer learning of the pretrained EVO model.
papers.abstract: The precise identification of promoters is crucial for understanding gene regulation. Deep learning methods have achieved considerable success in promoter prediction, yet most operate at the sequence level with coarse-grained labels. This means they label an entire DNA segment as either a "promoter" or "non-promoter," which results in a lack of the nucleotide-level resolution in prediction. In this study, we propose EvoSNR-Prom, a model designed for promoter prediction at single-nucleotide resolution. EvoSNR-Prom is built on the Evo foundation model and formulates promoter identification as a
papers.summary: EvoSNR-Prom is a new deep learning model that predicts promoters at single-nucleotide resolution, overcoming the limitations of existing sequence-level approaches that only provide coarse-grained labels. By leveraging the Evo foundation model and label-aware transfer learning, it achieves precise nucleotide-level promoter identification, which could improve the understanding of gene regulation.

papers.title: Integrating multi-layer perceptron and random forest in an ensemble framework for improved genomic prediction accuracy and SHAP-derived interpretability of residual feed intake in cattle.
papers.abstract: Feed efficiency (FE) is recognized as a vital component of sustainable dairy production, with residual feed intake (RFI) serving as a key metabolic indicator of FE independent of production levels. However, the genetic improvement of this complex trait is limited by the inability of conventional genomic Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (gBLUP) model to capture complex, non-linear genetic architectures and epistatic interactions. To address these limitations, this study aims to compare the predictive performance of machine learning (ML) approaches, specifically Random Forest (RF) and Multi-Layer
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study evaluates an ensemble machine learning framework combining Random Forest and Multi-Layer Perceptron for genomic prediction of residual feed intake in cattle, showing improved accuracy over conventional gBLUP. The authors also use SHAP values to interpret the model, identifying key genomic markers influencing feed efficiency, which could aid in genetic improvement of dairy cattle.

papers.title: Integrated Identification of NAD⁺ Metabolism-Associated Candidate Genes.
papers.abstract: Migraine is one of the most disabling neurological diseases globally; however, a significant proportion of patients do not respond to current treatments, or treatment efficacy diminishes over time, highlighting the need to identify additional molecular candidates for further investigation. Recent studies have increasingly focused on the role of neuro-immune interactions in migraine. This study aimed to identify peripheral immune-related candidate genes associated with NAD+ metabolism-related transcriptional features in migraine through integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses. U
papers.summary: This study identifies NAD+ metabolism-associated candidate genes in migraine by integrating bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses, focusing on peripheral immune-related mechanisms. The findings provide new molecular candidates for migraine research, potentially informing future therapeutic targets.

papers.title: An Explanatory Deep Learning Pipeline for the Prediction and Visualization of Spatially Resolved Biomarker Expression in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Histopathologic evaluation remains central to cancer diagnosis and treatment planning, yet the molecular programs underlying distinct tissue morphologies aren't routinely accessible in clinical workflows. Spatial transcriptomic/proteomic platforms provide region-specific molecular measurements but are limited by cost, throughput, and scalability. Most computational pathology models rely on either bulk tissue-based gene expression or a focused gene/protein expression-panel prediction, thereby obscuring subregion-specific morpho-molecular relationships and limiting spatial interpretation of a wi
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning pipeline that predicts spatially resolved biomarker expression in triple-negative breast cancer from histopathology images, enabling visualization of molecular patterns without costly spatial transcriptomic assays. The approach addresses the scalability limitations of spatial omics by linking tissue morphology to regional molecular programs, potentially improving clinical accessibility of molecular information.

papers.title: A genome-wide coverage-based pipeline for the identification of host-derived candidate biomarkers in blood cell-free DNA.
papers.abstract: We have created a new data-analysis pipeline for the discovery of host-derived candidate biomarkers in blood cell-free DNA sequencing data. Unlike approaches that rely on specific molecular or genetic signatures, our method leverages the coverage distribution of cell-free DNA sequences mapped to a reference genome, applying statistical analyses to identify informative short genomic regions for biomarker discovery. The pipeline is applicable to diverse diseases and can be used to analyze cell-free DNA sequences from plasma or serum to identify candidate biomarkers that are characteristic of dis
papers.summary: The authors developed a new bioinformatics pipeline that identifies host-derived candidate biomarkers from blood cell-free DNA sequencing data by analyzing genome-wide coverage patterns rather than relying on specific molecular or genetic signatures. The method uses statistical analyses of coverage distribution to pinpoint informative short genomic regions, making it applicable across diverse diseases and sample types such as plasma or serum.

papers.title: PlantCAD2: A DNA foundation model for interpreting genomes across flowering plants.
papers.abstract: Flowering plants (angiosperms) exhibit extraordinary species diversity, ∼200-fold variation in genome size, and relatively compact coding regions, presenting both a unique challenge and opportunity for DNA language models. Here, we introduce PlantCAD2, an extended-context, plant-specific DNA language model with single-nucleotide resolution, pre-trained on 65 angiosperm genomes, together with a series of public benchmarks for evaluation. Comprehensive zero-shot testing shows that PlantCAD2 (676 million parameters) efficiently captures evolutionary conservation, surpassing the 7-billion-paramete
papers.summary: PlantCAD2 is a new DNA foundation model pre-trained on 65 flowering plant genomes that captures evolutionary conservation and genomic features at single-nucleotide resolution, outperforming much larger models in zero-shot tasks. It provides public benchmarks and demonstrates that a plant-specific, extended-context model can efficiently interpret angiosperm genomes despite their size and diversity.

papers.title: Global observational analysis of the Quality of Care Index (QCI) for protein-energy malnutrition from 1990 to 2021.
papers.abstract: Protein-energy malnutrition (PEM) remains a critical global health challenge, and the quality of care for PEM remains a key focus in the current public health field. Systematically evaluating these disparities is essential for guiding public health policy. This study adopted a revised Quality of Care Index (QCI) to evaluate global PEM care performance from 1990 to 2021. This study is based on data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 1990 to 2021. The 4 secondary indicators were integrated through principal component analysis (PCA) to construct the QCI. The machine learning interpretability
papers.summary: This study uses a revised Quality of Care Index (QCI) to evaluate global care for protein-energy malnutrition from 1990 to 2021, based on Global Burden of Disease data. The authors integrate four indicators via principal component analysis and apply machine learning interpretability to assess disparities, aiming to inform public health policy.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted prediction of 5-year mortality in chronic kidney disease: the KoreaN cohort study for Outcome in patients With Chronic Kidney Disease (KNOW-CKD).
papers.abstract: Mortality prediction models for patients with non-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain limited despite their clinical importance. While machine learning (ML) offers the potential to improve prediction accuracy, its "black-box" nature has hindered clinical adoption. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable ML model for predicting 5-year all-cause mortality in patients with non-dialysis CKD and to deploy it as a user-friendly web-based risk stratification tool.
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable machine learning model to predict 5-year all-cause mortality in patients with non-dialysis chronic kidney disease, using data from the Korean KNOW-CKD cohort. The model was deployed as a user-friendly web-based tool, addressing the 'black-box' concern by providing interpretability for clinical adoption.

papers.title: From linear models to deep learning: statistical advances in genomic selection for animal breeding.
papers.abstract: Genomic selection (GS) has revolutionized animal breeding by accelerating genetic gain through genome-wide marker data. As genotyping technologies advance and data dimensionality grows, the statistical foundations of GS are shifting from classical linear frameworks, which assume additive genetic effects, toward advanced computational models that capture complex nonlinear relationships in genomic data. The commercialization of genotyping arrays for livestock and poultry, coupled with steadily declining sequencing costs, has led to an exponential increase in the availability of high-density geno
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This review discusses the evolution of statistical methods for genomic selection in animal breeding, from classical linear models to advanced deep learning approaches that can capture complex nonlinear relationships in high-dimensional genomic data. It highlights how advances in genotyping technologies and declining sequencing costs are driving this methodological shift.

papers.title: Experimental Investigation of Thermally Induced Stress Shadow Effects in Multiwell Hydraulic Fracturing and Neural-Network-Based Fracture Identification.
papers.abstract: Efficient stimulation of deep high-temperature, low-permeability reservoirs critically depends on the creation of complex fracture networks via multiwell hydraulic fracturing, where thermally induced stress shadow effects modulate fracture propagation and connectivity. In this study, we present a comprehensive experimental investigation using a self-developed high-temperature true triaxial multiwell fracturing apparatus and an artificial dual-well model to systematically characterize the coupled influence of the temperature field, perforation spacing, and fracturing sequence on fracture intera
papers.summary: This study experimentally investigates how thermally induced stress shadows affect fracture propagation in multiwell hydraulic fracturing, using a high-temperature triaxial apparatus and dual-well models. It also applies a neural network to identify fractures from experimental data, providing insights for optimizing stimulation in deep, high-temperature reservoirs.

papers.title: Polus: a context-aware enhancement framework for DNA storage via transformer-based soft-decision decoding.
papers.abstract: DNA storage offers exceptional information density and archival longevity but is constrained by complex biochemical noise inherent to synthesis, storage, and sequencing. Conventional hard-decision error-correction schemes often rely on excessive redundancy to mitigate these imperfections, which significantly compromises storage efficiency and density.
papers.summary: Polus is a new framework that uses a transformer-based soft-decision decoder to improve error correction in DNA storage systems. By leveraging context-aware information, it reduces the need for excessive redundancy, thereby enhancing storage efficiency and density while maintaining data integrity.

papers.title: The limits of bio-molecular modeling with large language models: a cross-scale evaluation.
papers.abstract: The modeling of bio-molecular system across molecular scales remains a central challenge in scientific research. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to bio-molecular discovery, yet systematic evaluation across multi-scale biological problems and rigorous assessment of their tool-augmented capabilities remain limited.
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates the performance of large language models (LLMs) across multiple scales of bio-molecular modeling, from molecular to systems level, and assesses the impact of tool augmentation. The findings reveal significant limitations in current LLMs for complex, multi-scale biological problems, highlighting where they fall short and where tool integration provides only partial improvement.

papers.title: EscaPRRS-ORF5: a structure-aware evolutionary framework for prioritizing immune escape-prone variants in porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus.
papers.abstract: Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome Virus (PRRSV) is a rapidly evolving RNA virus causing significant economic losses, posing a formidable challenge to vaccine efficacy due to its high mutational variability and immune escape. As the viral mutants evolve, their ability to sustain in population is driven by a range of host biology factors such as receptor binding, fusion, and uncoating. Existing tools that predict viral fitness and escape propensities rely heavily on extensive, up-to-date sequence data and lack integration of biochemical host interactions, limiting mechanistic underst
papers.summary: This paper introduces EscaPRRS-ORF5, a new computational framework that integrates structural information and host-virus interaction data to predict immune escape-prone variants in PRRSV. The approach addresses limitations of existing tools that rely only on sequence data, offering a more mechanistic way to prioritize viral mutants that may evade immunity.

papers.title: Deep learning for optoacoustic imaging of reversibly switchable proteins: training and performance testing using simulated multispectral optoacoustic tomography images.
papers.abstract: Reversibly switchable optoacoustic proteins (rsOAPs) are a promising candidate for sensitive and quantitative optoacoustic (OA) imaging of genetically modified cell populations, such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cells used in cancer immunotherapy. Although detection of rsOAPs has been demonstrated using classical machine learning approaches, there is still a need for higher detection sensitivity and more accurate quantification.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning approach for detecting and quantifying reversibly switchable optoacoustic proteins (rsOAPs) in multispectral optoacoustic tomography images, using simulated training data to improve sensitivity and accuracy over classical machine learning methods. The approach aims to enhance imaging of genetically modified cell populations, such as CAR T-cells in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Predictors of Failure After Two-Stage Revision for Periprosthetic Joint Infections of the Knee.
papers.abstract: Prosthetic joint infection (PJI) following total knee arthroplasty remains a serious complication. Although two-stage revision is considered the gold standard, predictors of failure remain unclear. This study aimed to identify factors associated with failure after two-stage revision for knee PJI using conventional statistics with exploratory machine-learning validation.
papers.summary: This study investigates factors associated with failure after two-stage revision surgery for prosthetic joint infections of the knee, using conventional statistics and exploratory machine learning. It aims to identify predictors that could help improve patient outcomes and guide clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Identification of obesity risk factors in 3-12-year-old children and adolescents with prior respiratory tract infections via interpretable machine and deep learning models.
papers.abstract: Childhood obesity and respiratory tract infections (RTIs) are 2 major global public health issues that frequently co-occur and are closely interrelated. Early detection of children with prior RTIs who are at high obesity risk is crucial for targeted interventions. This study integrates interpretable machine learning (ML) models and a deep learning network to develop an obesity risk prediction model in a large pediatric cohort.
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable machine learning and deep learning model to predict obesity risk in children aged 3-12 years with a history of respiratory tract infections, using a large pediatric cohort. The model identifies key risk factors, enabling early detection and targeted interventions for high-risk children.

papers.title: Meta-PseU: A meta-classifier for robust prediction of RNA pseudouridine modification sites from long sequences.
papers.abstract: Pseudouridine (Ψ) represents one of the most abundant and conserved RNA modifications. Ψ provides an additional hydrogen-bond donor that enhances RNA structural stability and modulates translation. It participates in diverse biological processes, including RNA-protein interactions, splicing, translational control, and stress responses. Aberrant pseudouridylation is implicated in cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, and autoimmune diseases. Despite its biological importance, experimental identification of Ψ sites remains time-consuming and costly, limiting the feasibility of transcriptome-wide
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This paper presents Meta-PseU, a meta-classifier that improves the prediction of RNA pseudouridine modification sites from long sequences by integrating multiple machine learning models. The tool aims to provide a more robust and accurate computational approach for identifying these important RNA modifications, which are implicated in various diseases.

papers.title: GeneInsight: Condensing gene set knowledge via language models.
papers.abstract: Gene set analysis often returns extensive annotations from multiple sources, requiring manual effort to identify coherent biological themes. We developed GeneInsight, an AI-powered tool that automates this by retrieving functional annotations from STRING-DB, clustering semantically related terms using sentence embeddings, and generating thematic summaries via large language model prompting. This enables researchers to identify biological themes that may be obscured when annotation sources are examined separately.
papers.summary: GeneInsight is an AI-powered tool that automates the interpretation of gene set analysis results by retrieving functional annotations from STRING-DB, clustering related terms, and generating thematic summaries using large language models. It helps researchers identify coherent biological themes that might be missed when examining annotation sources separately.

papers.title: The Sydney Triage to Admission Risk Tool With Artificial Intelligence (START-AI) to Support Decision Making in Emergency Departments: Model Explainability and Feature Importance Analysis.
papers.abstract: Evaluate the importance of specific variables contributing to a recently reported Artificial Intelligence (AI) prediction model called Sydney Triage to Admission Risk Tool with Artificial Intelligence (START-AI) to predict inpatient admission from the Emergency Department (ED).
papers.summary: This study analyzes the Sydney Triage to Admission Risk Tool with Artificial Intelligence (START-AI), an AI model that predicts whether emergency department patients will be admitted as inpatients, focusing on which variables most influence its predictions. The authors provide an explainability analysis to identify key features, aiming to support clinical decision-making by making the model's reasoning transparent.

papers.title: Drug sensitivity prediction across cancer types using graph isomorphism networks and biological pathway features: A dual-branch deep learning approach.
papers.abstract: Drug sensitivity prediction is an important issue within the precision medicine field. IC50, which is the molar drug dose needed to decrease the viability of cells by half compared to the drug-free control, is the main pharmacodynamics parameter used for drug sensitivity analysis in large-scale pharmacogenomics screenings. Computational estimation of IC50s based on molecular and genomic factors significantly reduces costs associated with experiments for measuring cell viability and allows for accelerating the process of drug discovery. Traditional methods of IC50 calculation do not allow integ
papers.summary: This paper presents a dual-branch deep learning model that combines graph isomorphism networks with biological pathway features to predict drug sensitivity (IC50) across multiple cancer types. The approach improves prediction accuracy by integrating molecular and genomic data, offering a cost-effective computational alternative to experimental drug sensitivity assays.

papers.title: Machine Learning Identified Mitophagy- and Hypoxia-Related Genes MTRNR2L8 and SUMO1P3 as Potential Biomarkers Associated with Unexplained Recurrent Pregnancy Loss.
papers.abstract: This study aims to identify mitophagy- and hypoxia-related biomarkers for unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss (uRPL) by integrating transcriptomic data with machine learning algorithms.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning on transcriptomic data to identify two genes, MTRNR2L8 and SUMO1P3, linked to mitophagy and hypoxia pathways as potential biomarkers for unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss (uRPL). These findings may improve diagnosis and understanding of the condition's molecular basis.

papers.title: Identification of endoplasmic reticulum stress-related biomarkers in asthma and asthma exacerbation.
papers.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress plays a crucial role in airway inflammation and other asthma-related processes. This study aims to identify potential ER stress-related biomarkers in asthma.
papers.summary: This study identifies potential endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress-related biomarkers associated with asthma and asthma exacerbation, highlighting their role in airway inflammation. The findings may offer new targets for diagnosis or therapy.

papers.title: Innovative digital twin framework for early risk detection and personalized perinatal healthcare.
papers.abstract: Pregnancy-related complications such as gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and preeclampsia require timely identification, as initially low-risk pregnancies may develop clinically relevant risks during follow-up. Digital Health and Telemedicine can support remote monitoring, while Digital Twin (DT) technology offers a framework for integrating longitudinal patient data with predictive models. However, DT-based perinatal systems remain exploratory and require methodological validation before clinical use.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a digital twin framework for perinatal healthcare that integrates longitudinal patient data with predictive models to enable early risk detection of complications like gestational diabetes and preeclampsia. The framework is designed for remote monitoring and personalized care, though the authors note that such systems require further methodological validation before clinical adoption.

papers.title: Identification and Experimental Validation of Key Lipid Metabolism-Related Genes in Intracerebral Hemorrhage Based on Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: The relationship between lipid metabolism and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is not fully understood, particularly regarding its potential contribution to disease initiation and progression. Accordingly, this study employed machine learning methods to identify and validate pivotal lipid metabolism-related genes in ICH.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to identify key lipid metabolism-related genes associated with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and validates them experimentally, providing new insights into the role of lipid metabolism in ICH pathogenesis. The findings may offer potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets for this condition.

papers.title: Machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome and carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an acquired autoimmune disorder characterized by recurrent vascular events in large, medium, or small vessels. These events contribute to cardiovascular disease primarily through thrombosis and atherosclerosis (AS). Carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) represents a particularly high-risk manifestation of subclinical AS in patients with APS. However, the shared molecular signatures linking APS and CAS remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify shared diagnostic genes and mechanistic links between antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and carotid atherosclerosis (CAS). The findings reveal common molecular signatures that may serve as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets for both conditions.

papers.title: An exploratory exome-wide machine learning analysis identifies candidate host gene signatures associated with Long COVID in a large admixed Brazilian cohort.
papers.abstract: Genetic factors have been suggested as modifiers of vulnerability to postCOVID-19 sequelae, referred to as Long COVID (LC). We hypothesize that LC may involve central nervous system (CNS)-related mechanisms, influenced by neuroinflammatory, autoimmune, viral mechanisms, and genetic factors. In this work, we used whole-exome sequencing in conjunction with a machine learning-based prioritization framework to investigate the connection between LC and host genomic variation.
papers.summary: This study uses whole-exome sequencing and machine learning to identify host genetic variants associated with Long COVID in a large Brazilian cohort, focusing on central nervous system-related mechanisms. The authors propose candidate gene signatures that may influence susceptibility to post-COVID sequelae, providing new insights into the genetic basis of Long COVID.

papers.title: Explainable XGBoost model and nomogram for risk factor identification and risk prediction in cerebral small vessel disease: a machine learning-based retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a common, clinically significant vascular disorder that frequently leads to cognitive impairment, dementia, and poor overall prognosis. Owing to its complex hemodynamic characteristics and multifactorial pathophysiology, early identification of individuals at high risk for CSVD remains a clinical challenge. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model for predicting the occurrence of CSVD.
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable machine learning model (XGBoost) with a nomogram to predict the risk of cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) and identify key risk factors. The model aims to improve early identification of high-risk individuals by providing a transparent, clinically usable tool.

papers.title: Data-augmented machine learning refines the effective-concentration estimate for eculizumab in complement-mediated diseases.
papers.abstract: Eculizumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the complement protein C5, is highly efficient in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome, generalized myasthenia gravis, and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder. However, recent reports have highlighted a subset of patients who show inadequate treatment response, prompting dose escalation or interval shortening. The serum concentration required for sustained inhibition of the complement lytic pathway remains uncertain, and the commonly cited 50-100 µg/ml range is not grounded in robust pharmacokinetic-pha
papers.summary: This study uses data-augmented machine learning to refine the effective serum concentration estimate for eculizumab, a complement inhibitor used in several rare diseases. The authors challenge the commonly cited 50-100 µg/ml range, suggesting a more precise target based on robust modeling. This could improve dosing strategies for patients with inadequate response.

papers.title: Machine learning and bioinformatics identify and validate membrane protein biomarkers for type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is among the most rapidly increasing metabolic disorders worldwide. Membrane proteins, integral components of biological membranes, are pivotal in insulin signal transduction and significantly contribute to the pathogenesis of T2DM. However, the systematic investigation of membrane proteins linked to T2DM remains insufficient.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and bioinformatics to identify and validate membrane protein biomarkers associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), addressing a gap in systematic investigation of these proteins in the disease. The findings highlight potential diagnostic or therapeutic targets, though specific results are not detailed in the abstract.

papers.title: Construction and optimization of a genomic selection model for total sugar content in tobacco.
papers.abstract: Total sugar is one of the chemical indicators related to tobacco quality. However, due to its composition of various oligosaccharides, disaccharides, and polysaccharides, total sugar lacks a clear genetic target, making conventional breeding approaches for its improvement particularly challenging. Therefore, conducting genomic selection (GS) studies on total sugar content holds significant importance for the development of high-sugar tobacco varieties. In this study, 2,604 tobacco germplasm accessions with broad genetic diversity, sourced from the National tobacco Germplasm Repository, were us
papers.summary: This study develops and optimizes a genomic selection model for total sugar content in tobacco using 2,604 diverse germplasm accessions. The work addresses the challenge of breeding for a complex trait with no clear genetic target, providing a practical tool for improving sugar content in tobacco varieties.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in haematology laboratory diagnosis: Current applications, challenges, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming haematology diagnostics by improving accuracy, efficiency, and reproducibility in workflows traditionally reliant on manual microscopy and expert interpretation. Integrating AI into laboratory medicine presents opportunities to enhance diagnostic precision and reduce variability, particularly in resource-limited settings.
papers.summary: This review examines the current applications, challenges, and future directions of artificial intelligence in haematology laboratory diagnosis, highlighting its potential to improve accuracy, efficiency, and reproducibility in workflows that traditionally depend on manual microscopy. It emphasizes opportunities for enhancing diagnostic precision and reducing variability, particularly in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Shared glycosylation-related molecular mechanism and immune infiltration patterns of fetal growth restriction and preeclampsia.
papers.abstract: Placental dysfunction and immune dysregulation are central to disorders such as fetal growth restriction (FGR) and preeclampsia (PE). Although aberrant placental glycosylation has been implicated in various pregnancy complications, the specific expression patterns of glycosylation-related genes (GRGs) associated with placental pathology and their potential role in driving immune imbalance at the maternal-fetal interface remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates the shared molecular mechanisms between fetal growth restriction (FGR) and preeclampsia (PE), focusing on glycosylation-related genes (GRGs) and immune infiltration patterns in the placenta. The authors identify common aberrant GRG expression and associated immune dysregulation, suggesting a shared glycosylation-related pathway contributing to placental dysfunction in both conditions.

papers.title: Instability of LLM text embeddings for unsupervised dimension reduction of tabular data.
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) text embeddings have recently been used for supervised learning on tabular data by serializing each observation into text and then converting the text into a dense fixed-length vector. This strategy is appealing for biomedical tabular data, which are often mixed-type and contain missing values, because it produces a complete numeric representation even when some original entries are missing. However, its suitability for unsupervised tasks remains unclear. Here we evaluate the use of LLM-derived text embeddings for dimension reduction of tabular data, focusing on biol
papers.summary: This study evaluates the use of LLM text embeddings for unsupervised dimension reduction of tabular biomedical data, finding that these embeddings are unstable for such tasks. The authors caution against relying on LLM embeddings for unsupervised analysis, despite their appeal for handling mixed-type and missing data.

papers.title: Clinical AI-assisted FXR prioritization and WADDAICA-guided design of a berberine-inspired analogue for MASH: integrated computational and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), lack effective targeted therapies despite increasing global prevalence. The farnesoid X receptor (FXR) is a key regulator of hepatic lipid metabolism, inflammation, and fibrosis, making it a promising therapeutic target. However, existing FXR modulators are associated with limited efficacy and adverse effects.
papers.summary: This study uses clinical AI-assisted prioritization of FXR as a therapeutic target for MASH and applies the WADDAICA computational framework to design a berberine-inspired analogue. The compound was validated experimentally, showing potential as a novel FXR modulator for treating MASH.

papers.title: Foundation model-enhanced multimodal radiomics for predicting response to chemo-immunotherapy in advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To develop and validate a foundation model-driven multimodal fusion framework for non-invasive prediction of treatment response to first-line chemo-immunotherapy in patients with advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC).
papers.summary: This study presents a foundation model-enhanced multimodal radiomics framework that non-invasively predicts treatment response to first-line chemo-immunotherapy in advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma. The approach integrates imaging and clinical data, showing potential for improving personalized treatment decisions.

papers.title: Pooling multimodal cancer data across unaligned embedding spaces maintains tumor of origin signal.
papers.abstract: AI-based embeddings offer the possibilities of encoding complex biological data into low-dimensional spaces, called embedding spaces, that maintain the relationships between entities. Vector pooling is the process of aggregating an array of embedded vectors, either usually by summing or averaging, to summarize the total movement with the embedding space. Embedded vector pooling allows sampling of an arbitrary number of points to be summarized into a fixed sized vector, and is frequently used to sample networks of embedded values or to summarize protein language model vectors. There is an open
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether pooling multimodal cancer data across unaligned embedding spaces preserves tumor-of-origin signal. The authors find that vector pooling methods can effectively aggregate embedded data from different modalities, maintaining the biological signal of tumor origin even when embedding spaces are not aligned.

papers.title: Object-centric diffusion policies for real-world robotic-arm imitation learning.
papers.abstract: Imitation learning in complex, unstructured environments remains challenging due to the difficulty of grounding perception in physically meaningful representations and the need to model multimodal action distributions. Existing approaches often rely on unstructured pixel-level feature encodings or stochastic latent-variable decoders, which can lead to brittle attention in cluttered scenes. In this work, we present a novel integration of detector-based visual representations with conditional diffusion modeling (DINO + CDP) for real-world robotic imitation learning. Our framework utilizes a DINO
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new approach for robotic imitation learning that combines detector-based visual representations (DINO) with conditional diffusion modeling to improve performance in cluttered, unstructured environments. The method addresses challenges of brittle attention and multimodal action distributions, showing promise for real-world robotic-arm tasks.

papers.title: mwHIT: accelerated and accurate histone modification imputation using multi-scale window attention.
papers.abstract: Histone modifications regulate chromatin organization and gene activity, and abnormal modification patterns are closely associated with disease-related transcriptional dysregulation. Although ChIP-seq provides accurate measurements of histone modification profiles, genome-wide experimental profiling remains costly and time-consuming. Here, we propose mwHIT, a multi-scale window attention-based Histone Modification Imputation Transformer that predicts histone modification signals from run-on sequencing (RO-seq) and DNA sequence features. mwHIT captures both local and long-range regulatory infor
papers.summary: mwHIT is a new deep-learning method that imputes histone modification signals from RO-seq and DNA sequence data using multi-scale window attention, capturing both local and long-range regulatory information. It offers a faster and more accurate alternative to experimental ChIP-seq profiling, potentially reducing cost and time in epigenomic studies.
